studyInfo.title: 2×2 Factorial User Experience & Fairness Perception Study
studyInfo.description: Simulated HCI evaluation comparing user trust, perceived fairness, and task efficiency across automated vs explainable and user-controlled allocation interfaces.
studyInfo.simulationNotice: Simulated prototype study results for research demonstration.

conditions.name: Black-Box Baseline (No Explanation, No Control)
conditions.summary: Users expressed high skepticism toward waitlist outcomes without explanations or alternative booking agency.

conditions.name: Transparent Passive (SHAP Explanation On, No Control)
conditions.summary: SHAP explanations significantly improved perceived fairness and algorithmic understanding, though users desired control to modify preferences.

conditions.name: Interactive Unexplained (No Explanation, Control On)
conditions.summary: Agency to re-request seats or select alternative trips improved satisfaction, but lack of transparency left reasons for initial waitlists unclear.

conditions.name: Full SmartBus System (SHAP Explanation On, Control On)
conditions.summary: Combining transparent XAI feature attributions with proactive user controls (alternative rebooking, review requests) achieved highest trust and system acceptance.
